text: A revenue problem is just a constraint you haven't named yet.

The most expensive number in a business is the one nobody's measuring.

Usually it's the conversion between two stages everyone assumes are fine.

Most owners think it's a lead problem.
Usually it's a follow-up problem.

The symptom is where it hurts. The constraint is where you fix it.

Growth has an order of operations:

1. Find the one constraint limiting everything else
2. Fix it until it's no longer the limit
3. Re-diagnose, the constraint has moved

Most businesses skip step 1 and wonder why effort doesn't turn into growth.

Every company has one constraint that limits everything else.

Right now it's usually one of:
• Retention
• Cash flow
• Sales conversion
• Delivery capacity

Find that one first. Everything downstream gets easier.

Revenue problems are usually symptoms.
Constraints are the disease.

Fastest way to waste a budget:

Scale before you diagnose.

Pricing is the fastest lever you have.

No new leads. No new headcount.
A 10% price increase drops almost straight to margin.

Most businesses are underpriced, because they never actually tested it.

Your content isn’t the problem.

Your distribution is.

Why great posts die and average posts win 👇

Most people spend 80% making the thing and 20% getting it seen.

Winners invert it: make it good enough, then spend the real effort on reach.
Reach levers nobody uses: strong first line, posting when your people are awake, replying to bigger accounts, and repurposing the same idea across platforms.
Same idea, 5 formats, 5 days. Keep the one that pops. Kill the rest. That’s a distribution system, not luck.

Creation gets you a post. Distribution gets you a business. Build the second one.

Save this. Follow for the rest of the system.

I turned a dead account around by changing one thing.

Not the topic. Not the frequency.

The first line 👇
parts:
I turned a dead account around by changing one thing.

Not the topic. Not the frequency.

The first line 👇

The posts were genuinely good. But every one opened with wallpaper — “Today I want to talk about…”

Nobody stops for a warm-up.

We rewrote only line one for a week:

• name the person
• name the pain
• promise the outcome

Same body copy underneath.

Stops tripled. Same content. The hook was the entire bottleneck.

Your best idea with a weak first line is a tree falling in an empty forest.

Rule: spend as long on line one as you spend on the other ten.

Save this. Follow for the rest of the system.
